active_themes.label: AI Trade Loses Its Shield
active_themes.summary: Today supplied the missing half of the stagflation picture: weak hiring (29,000 jobs, unemployment up to 4.2%) alongside an inflation surge. Low layoffs and jobless claims near multi-decade lows mean employers are not firing, just not hiring, so this looks like a frozen labor market rather than a collapsing one. The Nasdaq's record close shows the AI trade is shielded again for now, but only because yields fell. Whether that holds depends on whether the Fed's attention stays on inflation or shifts to jobs.

active_themes.label: The Fix Unwound
active_themes.summary: US bond yields fell on the jobs miss, giving back a little of the global sell-off that pushed US government borrowing costs to their highest since 2002. A Fed pause only addresses part of that story, because the long-term yield spike has also been about government deficits. No confirmed 10-year close is in hand, so the 5.25% and 5% thresholds stay open.

active_themes.label: Talks Over Tankers
active_themes.summary: Oil fell more than 2% on talk of releasing diesel and crude stockpiles, even as new US sanctions hit Iran's auto and rail sectors and the blockade keeps squeezing shipping lanes. The price drop comes from supply-side relief talk, not from any confirmed easing at sea. No Brent level or Hormuz traffic print is confirmed, so the oil verdict stays open.

active_themes.label: Fed Voices Split
active_themes.summary: The Fed's internal watchdog found no criminal wrongdoing in the Powell-era renovation cost overruns. That removes a legal pretext Trump used in his pressure campaign against Powell. There is still no concrete action against Warsh or other officials over the Fed vote. The open question is whether the pressure moves from words to action.

open_watchlist.condition: UK diesel closes above £2 a litre for the first time.
open_watchlist.meaning: Energy costs are feeding through to household budgets, which keeps central banks wary of easing.

open_watchlist.condition: The FTC's AI safety probe produces formal demands or a named target among the large AI companies.
open_watchlist.meaning: Regulatory risk is now landing on the sector carrying the market, which raises the cost of a tech slip.

open_watchlist.condition: The UK 30-year gilt yield (UK government 30-year bond) closes above 6%, rather than only touching it during the day.
open_watchlist.meaning: A close, not a spike, would show the global bond sell-off has real staying power and that mortgage and borrowing costs will keep rising.

open_watchlist.condition: The S&P 500 falls 1% or more on a day when US government yields rise.
open_watchlist.meaning: Stocks would be admitting that the bond move matters, ending the calm that held today.

open_watchlist.condition: A formal government announcement of a diesel or crude stockpile release.
open_watchlist.meaning: That would turn today's talk into real supply and give oil a firmer reason to stay lower, easing inflation pressure.

open_watchlist.condition: The next Nationwide reading shows UK house prices falling for a second straight month.
open_watchlist.meaning: It would confirm that higher bond yields are feeding through to household budgets, not just to markets.

open_watchlist.condition: The Fed raises rates at its meeting this month.
open_watchlist.meaning: It would mean inflation outweighed the jobs miss, and today's rally priced the wrong outcome.

open_watchlist.condition: The next unemployment reading comes in at 4.3% or higher.
open_watchlist.meaning: Two straight upticks would suggest a real softening rather than a one-month wobble, moving the Fed debate toward growth.

open_watchlist.condition: The next consumer price report shows annual inflation higher than the prior reading.
open_watchlist.meaning: Weak jobs with accelerating prices is the stagflation squeeze, and the market's bad-news-is-good-news logic would break.

open_watchlist.condition: Fed officials publicly say the September jobs miss does not change the case for raising rates.
open_watchlist.meaning: It would show the hike is still live and that today's relief rally rests on a hope the Fed isn't sharing.
